items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: In Benny’s band as you know, Lionel Hampton

ctx.x: You witnessed some of the changes in the segregation between the blacks and whites in music.

Well let’s see. In Benny’s band as you know, Lionel Hampton and I don’t know — in 1951 I opened the Embers, I had Buck Clayton — oddly enough I had three black guys with me. Milt Hinton, Buck Clayton and Jo Jones. Later on Johnny Smith. Buck had to do some stuff with Count Basie again and Johnny Smith came in and played with us so we were split equally, two white and two colored. And as a young kid, or going to school, there was always deep segregation. And as a matter of fact, a thing that Milt Hinton was…
You were involved in one of Bing Crosby’s last recording too, weren’t you? It was around ’76 or so?
